items.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025
items.q: And him and Quincy Jones especially, did a lot of stuff together.

ctx.x: That’s such an interesting thing for you to say, and hard to explain to – like his intent, his message. You feel the need to really listen to what – and I don't know how you can explain how you could do that. Can you do it on purpose or is it just in him?

Well I think both. I think both. If he sensed – well he was a guy, you know that school, that generation of players, if you didn’t know your bridge or something he would humiliate you on the bandstand. You know? He would say nasty things in front of the audience to you, and you would shrink you know, but that’s the way they were you know. They were tough that way. So you didn’t want to play a tune you didn’t know along with him. But yeah, his strength, just all the years and experience he played, you know he was…
What were the – were there down years and up years or parts of decades that you could make a living – I won’t say easier, I don’t think it’s ever easy –
